title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Possible inconsistency with the previous page: there SN*_ρ is identified with Cent_{𝔖^+}(ρ), while the margin here gives its image as Norm_{𝔖^+}(L_ρ). These agree only under hypotheses such as ρ² ≠ 1 and self-normalizing behaviour; Grothendieck himself hedges with 'si ρ² ≠ 1'.

Surjectivity of δ_ρ, δ_σ onto Γ_{ρ,σ} is asserted 'de façon évidente'. It depends on how Γ_{ρ,σ} was defined on earlier pages: every element of Γ must lift to an element normalizing L_ρ. This cannot be checked from this page alone.
Notation drifts between N_ρ, N*_ρ, SN_ρ and SN*_ρ, and between Z_ρ and N*_ρ. Grothendieck flags this himself in the previous page's NB.

ideas.what: Presenting normalizers of inertia/torsion subgroups as extensions of a common arithmetic quotient Γ by their intersection with the geometric group, mapping into the global extension 1→𝔖^+→G→Γ→1
ideas.modern_name: decomposition-group-type extensions: normalizers of inertia in an outer Galois action, split relative to the arithmetic quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard anabelian/GT technique (Ihara, Nakamura, Drinfeld's GT, Lochak–Schneps for PSL2-type GT work)
ideas.where_published: Spirit is in La Longue Marche (1981) and Esquisse d'un programme; these specific diagrams unsure

ideas.what: Cyclotomic-type characters χ_ρ = χ∘δ_ρ on the normalizers, with kernels N*^+
ideas.modern_name: restriction of the cyclotomic character to decomposition/normalizer groups

ideas.what: Sign characters ε recording the action on the inertia L_σ when restricted to the normalizer of the other point ρ, expected to be surjective on Z_ρ in 'good cases'
ideas.modern_name: orientation/sign characters on normalizers of torsion elements (e.g. action on elliptic points of order 2, 3 in PSL2)

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open the study of the cross sign composites N*_ρ → Γ → {±1} (via ε_{γ,σ}) and N*_σ → Γ → {±1} (via ε_{γ,ρ}). He asserts only that in 'good cases' their restrictions to Z_ρ, Z_σ are surjective, without defining the 'good cases' on this page.
missed.quote: Il faudrait encore examiner les composés (49) ... on verra que dans les "bons cas", la restriction de ces hom. à Z_ρ, Z_σ respectivement sont épi
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor technical point inside a bookkeeping construction. It might matter only to someone reconstructing Grothendieck's treatment of the loop equation in the archive.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine notational and bookkeeping step: exact sequences, injectivity of inclusions, composite characters and their kernels. The only open item is a small technical NB; nothing appears new relative to the GT/anabelian literature.
transcription_corrections: The quotient group written 'γ_{ρ,σ}' throughout should be Γ_{ρ,σ}, consistent with the previous page and diagram (45). The handwritten capital gamma resembles a lowercase γ.
Marginal phrase '(en commun, si ρ̂²≠1 ...)' is uncertain. It may read '(en tout cas, si ρ² ≠ 1 resp. σ² ≠ 1)'; the hats on ρ, σ are doubtful.
In (48), the second line is χ_σ = χ_γ∘δ_σ (the δ subscript was corrected in the manuscript), with the overwritten N*_σ as source.
'qui en général diffèrent de ceux-ci' — the reading 'diffèrent' is plausible; the original has 'différent'.
